rationales.1: The short-version box is an explicit scannable alternative and the prose plus ledger table deliver the finding without chart decoding.
rationales.2: Gaps are drawn as gaps, the method change is a dotted line, and the truncated 550 to 750 bar axis is labeled, but the charts are small with near-illegible axis text and the storm year is highlighted without its caveat.
rationales.3: The 2019 reading of 132 millimetres is stamped with an affirmative VERIFIED badge and appears in the ledger with no qualifying note, directly falsifying the required unverified label; the other disclosures being present cannot rescue an inverted one.
rationales.4: The gardener opening and the paperwork fragments hit the local register, though headers like the hardest day in the book tip toward drama the record does not need.
rationales.5: Competent typography but small body text, undersized charts in a wide canvas, and looser polish than the other three candidates.
rationales.6: A linear readable document with no visible scroll-driven pacing or apparatus.
rationales.7: This is a well-organized article about the data rather than a form that is the journalism; no single idea binds content, visuals, and mechanics.
rationales.8: Mechanics stay conventional and nothing exceeds the break budget, but no deliberate declared break exists either, leaving it professionally plain.
rationales.9: The voice is mostly sober and local, yet the storm treatment reads more like a weather feature any paper could run.
rationales.10: The hero moment of the page, the badged 132 millimetre stat, is built on the one reading the dataset explicitly does not stand behind, which is the effect-detached-from-reporting failure this criterion exists to catch.
